headline: Oil falls more than 4% on hopes the Doha Hormuz talks ease supply disruption
dek: Oil fell more than 4% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran raised hopes Middle East supply disruptions could ease. This extends the morning's >3% fall recorded at 09:45 (AJ liveblog) into a >4% move, and sits alongside the Dawn…
fault_line: Is the >4% oil drop a real peace signal, or a hopes rally that one strike headline reverses?

sections.what_happened: Oil fell more than 4% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran raised hopes Middle East supply disruptions could ease. This extends the morning's >3% fall recorded at 09:45 (AJ liveblog) into a >4% move, and sits alongside the Dawn liveblog's in-window restatement (14:14 ) that Iranian negotiators left Doha Sunday with a draft proposal circulating and a follow-up meeting possible -- the draft substance itself was already recorded at 1200. Treat the >4% print as the only incremental number in this liveblog sequence.
sections.what_verified: Reuters via Dawn liveblog; morning AJ liveblog print (>3%) is the same wire direction, not a second family for the >4% figure.
sections.what_disputed: The price move is hopes-driven, not deal-driven: Washington has not accepted the two-day plan, Araghchi said Nov 1 the Doha consultations reached no conclusion, and the OFAC toll warning (1500-01) shows the sanctions/shipping confrontation hardening in parallel. A hopes rally can reverse on one headline.
sections.why_matters: Update-detail only: fold the >4% print into the Hormuz-talks item as the market's vote on the draft proposal -- not a standalone Short.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW MARKET UPDATE-DETAIL to 1200-01 (Dawn liveblog 03:36pm PKT = 14:36 , Reuters) -- Oil falls more than 4% on hopes the Doha Hormuz talks ease supply disruption

totw_analysis: Our read: Update-detail only: fold the >4% print into the Hormuz-talks item as the market's vote on the draft proposal -- not a standalone Short. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the >4% oil drop a real peace signal, or a hopes rally that one strike headline reverses?
